finding: Item 7's negative ("and no §2.3 warning") is still vacuous under the fixture item 7 itself states, and it is now the ONLY assertion anywhere in §6 that would exercise §2.6's new buffering rule — the whole mechanism this round's repair introduced. The fixture is "Deactivating every role of a phase": such a spec names only real, active ids, so no unknown-id warning is producible, and nothing in the fixture involves `domain`, so no domain-filtering warning is producible either. Per §2.6 the §2.3 warnings are exactly those two producers, so under this fixture no §2.3 warning exists to be suppressed and the assertion passes in every implementation — including one that writes the warnings straight through before exiting 2, which is precisely what §2.6 forbids. The round-8 resolution ("§6 item 7's negative is no longer vacuous — it asserts the absence of a §2.3 warning, which §2.6's buffering rule makes a real behaviour to test") mistakes the rule for the fixture: buffering makes suppression observable only in a run that actually produces a warning. Third round running that this exact vacuity is reported and recorded as cured. Item 7's other two assertions (message on stderr, empty stdout) and the per-command artifact sets ARE non-vacuous — only the warning half is dead.

finding: The unchanged §2.2 (line 38) still says `ResolveOverrideFocus` "reads it and emits the \"matches no active role\" warning itself", which is the sentence round 8's high at index 0 cited as the reason the buffering could not hold. So the only sentence in the spec that assigns the warning to a component says the resolver writes it, while the only sentence that describes the mechanism says nothing is written until the checks are decided in the callers (§2.3 line 44 puts both refusals at the two CLI callers).
